ai.description: *Walkerana muduga* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It features a pointed snout, granular skin, and long, slender limbs adapted for leaping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Walkerana muduga* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored lateral band extending from the snout through the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Walkerana muduga* inhabits high-altitude evergreen shola forests and rocky stream banks in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Muduga mountain leaping frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky stream banks of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Walkerana muduga* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying clutches of 15–30 eggs in rock crevices or damp moss near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Walkerana muduga* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Walkerana muduga* emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink" notes, typically heard while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing streams in mountain forests.
